subject: OTLP Edge Proxy certification with Datadog & Grafana - technical validation plan
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-25T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: OTLP Edge proxy cert - intro and proposed scope

Sooj, team —

Following up from last week's partner sync: Datadog and Grafana asked for a lightweight certification plan for our new OTLP Edge Proxy (v0.9) so they can formally list it as a supported ingestion path for customers using managed agents. EdgeOps (our consultancy partner) will run the lab validation.

Proposed scope (high level):
- Functional: OTLP/gRPC + OTLP/HTTP export (TLS mTLS), batching, resource attributes preserved
- Observability: trace/span attributes, metric consistency, delta/monotonic counter handling
- Compatibility checks: Datadog agent v7.42 receiver, Grafana Tempo/Loki ingestion
- Scale: synthetic load up to 10k spans/sec for 15m windows

Attached is the draft cert plan (otlp-cert-plan-v2.pdf). Can Marcus and Hannah validate the test list and owner matrix? I'll coordinate scheduling with Amit and Lisa.

Thanks,
Camila
Partner Programs | Redwood Inference

Attachments: otlp-cert-plan-v2.pdf

From: Amit Patel <amit@datadog.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeOps Consulting <partners@edgeops.io>
Date: 2026-11-25T12:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: OTLP Edge proxy cert - intro and proposed scope

Thanks Camila — this looks reasonable. A couple of notes from the Datadog side:

- For spans, we need stable service.name + span.kind mapping; please ensure resource.attributes.service.name is set by the proxy when missing.
- Sampling: confirm whether client-side sampling flags are propagated (we expect a sample_rate attribute).
- Auth/TLS: we will provide a test CA and expect the proxy to accept mTLS from our agent; lab will test both mTLS and plain TLS.
- Metric mapping: we will validate that OTLP gauge/summary histograms translate to Datadog metric types without cardinality explosions.

Happy to jump on a quick tech call Wed 11/27. Amit
Datadog Integrations

---
On Wed, Nov 25, 2026 at 09:12 AM Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Sooj, team —
> ...

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Patel <amit@datadog.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-26T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: OTLP Edge proxy cert - intro and proposed scope

Amit — thanks, noted. A few implementation clarifications from our side:

1) service.name fallback: current proxy will set service.name from the first resource attribute or fallback to "redwood-edge-proxy". We'll add an explicit config option to prefer incoming resource.service.name.
2) Sampling flags: the proxy preserves trace flags and will add sample_rate as an attribute when configured to do so. We'll include a test that toggles this behavior.
3) TLS: we have two modes in CI — agent-auth (mTLS) and gateway-only (server TLS). EdgeOps will run both modes.

I've updated the test matrix in the attached configs (dd-grafana-sample-configs.tar.gz). Marcus
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Attachments: dd-grafana-sample-configs.tar.gz

From: EdgeOps Consulting <partners@edgeops.io>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Amit Patel <amit@datadog.com>, Lisa Wong <lisa@grafana.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-27T11:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: OTLP Edge proxy cert - lab schedule and test harness

Hi all —

We spun up the lab cluster and validated baseline connectivity. Quick summary of scheduled runs:
- 2026-11-29 09:00 PST: functional pass (TLS/mTLS, attribute mapping)
- 2026-11-29 12:00 PST: throughput run (5k spans/sec for 30m)
- 2026-11-30 10:00 PST: long-tail and delta metrics check

Preliminary blocker: Grafana Tempo ingestion failed intermittently when span batch sizes hit >1000; we suspect backpressure handling in the proxy. We'll attach detailed logs after the throughput run.

Regards,
Maya Rao | EdgeOps Consulting

Attachment: edgeproxy-test-results.csv

From: Lisa Wong <lisa@grafana.com>
To: EdgeOps Consulting <partners@edgeops.io>, Amit Patel <amit@datadog.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T15:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: OTLP Edge proxy cert - lab schedule and test harness

Thanks Maya — the intermittent failures match what we saw in an internal test last month. A couple requests from Grafana Tempo team: 

- Can you enable per-batch size throttling to cap at 500 and measure end-to-end latencies? Tempo's ingestion path is vulnerable to large burst batches.
- Include trace IDs in the failure logs and an example of the malformed batch payload so our ingestion team can reproduce locally.

I've cc'd our integrations engineer David (david@grafana.com) for follow-up. We'll try a quick replay once you have logs.

— Lisa
Partner Success, Grafana

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Patel <amit@datadog.com>, Lisa Wong <lisa@grafana.com>, EdgeOps Consulting <partners@edgeops.io>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: OTLP Edge proxy cert - final notes and next steps

Hi all —

Thanks for the rapid turnaround and the detailed test artifacts. Summary and next steps: 

- Marcus will push a patch today to enforce default batch cap at 500 and add opt-in telemetry for backend backpressure (feature flag).
- EdgeOps to re-run the throughput window tomorrow using the patched proxy and deliver the full replay and trace IDs to Lisa/David. Expected reschedule: 2026-12-01 09:00 PST.
- Camila and I will coordinate partner listing copy and the small legal checklist for "supported" designation.

If there are no further technical objections, Datadog/Grafana teams should be comfortable with a conditional pass after the re-run. I'll update the Confluence plan and close the JIRA when EdgeOps uploads the final CSV.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0192
